- Villa St. Joseph - $651,244 in HOME, $576,000 in former Redevelopment Set-Aside, and $372,756 in in-lieu fees
- Katella terrace - $780,000 in HOME Funds
Additionally, to keep their costs low, the City paid for the Subsidy Layering Analysis and NEPA required by HUD for both projects. 

In 2022 the City used its CDBG funds for projects supporting programs that include street improvements, handicap accessibility improvements, after-school programs, transitional housing, and supportive services in disadvantaged areas of the City. In future years, the City intends to allocate funds supporting home rehabilitation in disadvantaged neighborhoods.

In 2022, the City continued to fund a collaboration with a number of neighboring Orange County cities, the City of Orange participates in the North Services Planning Area (SPA) partnership. The North SPA Partnership is a joint collaboration that includes two full-service Navigation Centers to provide help to the region’s homeless – the Buena Park Center and the Placentia Center will provide homeless individuals a total of 250 beds, health resources, job skill training, and the ability to reconnect with lost family. In addition to participating in the North SPA, Orange has undertaken several other initiatives over the past few years to address local homelessness issue; including partnering with HomeAid of Orange County to develop the Orange Family Care Center. families who are experiencing homelessness and has over 55 beds.

and agencies.

The City understands that overly-restrictive development standards, burdensome entitlement processes and unreasonable development fees can pose a significant barrier to future residential development. As such, the City adopted a Code Streamlining and Improvement Program to strategically evaluate and amend the Zoning Code on a continuous basis in response to market and business trends. The 2024 Code Streamlining Zoning Code Amendment amended various chapters of Title 18 (Zoning) of the Anaheim Municipal Code (“Code”) to increase efficiency, improve service delivery, and respond to changing regulatory and market demands.Specific amendments include:                                                                   
• Accessory Dwelling Units (ADU):Provides consistency with State Law which permits ADUs both within and detached from multi-family dwellings and increases the maximum detached ADUs from two (2) to eight (8) for existing multi-family dwellings so long as the number of detached ADUs do not exceed the number of existing multiple-family residential units.  
• Fences and Walls: Provides regulatory relief by increasing the maximum height of fencing allowed within the required side, rear, or interior setbacks from 6 feet to 8 feet in all zones.                                                                                                   • Affordable Housing: Refers directly to State Law with respect to density bonus and other incentives and provides a cross-reference to Inclusionary Housing requirements.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         These amendments were adopted by City Council on January 14, 2025 and went into effect on Feb 13, 2025.

PROGRAM_STATUS: The City of Anaheim established a process to prioritize water and sewer improvements associated with affordable housing development. In April, 2007, the City Council adopted Resolution 2007-040 to grant priority for the provision of available and future resources or services to proposed housing developments that help meet the City’s share of the regional housing needs for lower income households as identified in the Housing Element and any amendments to the Housing Element. If the City’s Urban Water Management Plan identifies the need for the Public Utilities Department to allocate water supplies in the future, priority for uncommitted water supplies will be granted to applications for water services for proposed developments that include housing units affordable for lower income households. In cases of insufficient sewer capacity for potential affordable housing development sites where funding is not immediately available to correct the deficiency, the City will work cooperatively with the applicant and all City staff to identify alternative solutions and methods to adequately serve the proposed project.  City staff will continue to seek opportunities to assist affordable housing developers in the provison of infrastructure to facilitate assist affordable housing development.

PROGRAM_STATUS: The City began the process to develop a specific plan and associated environmental documents for the re-use of the Fairview Development site as affordable and market rate housing (at least 2,300 units) in 2022 when the City and State entered into an agreement and received grant funds. In 2025, the State extended the contract term to end on December 31, 2026. The City retained the professional services of Placeworks and initiated the Fairview Developmental Center (FDC) Specific Plan project in 2023. The current phase of the project generally includes the preparation of a specific plan and associated environmental review for the re-use of the site with a range of affordable and market rate housing. Technical studies have been completed and the City continues to hold bi-weekly coordination meetings with the State Department of General Services (DGS) and Department of Development Services (DDS). Staff and Placeworks have coordinated and hosted 18 community outreach events on the visioning and land use framework, as well as land use concepts, mobility, and urban design in 2023 and 2024. City Council provided a recommendation on the preferred plan for environmental study purposes for the Specific Plan on October 21, 2025. Following the hearing, staff issued a Notice of Preparation and held a scoping meeting on November 17th, 2025. PROGRAM_NAME: Monitoring and Preservation of At‐Risk Housing Units

As these units are no longer at risk of converting to market rate, this Housing Element program is considered complete.

PROGRAM_STATUS: In 2022, the City adopted mixed-use zoning district standards and rezoned portion of the City to higher density mixed-use zoning.   These mixed-use areas include the city’s most prominent transit corridors.  In addition to adopting higher density zoning for residential use, the City has also adopted a Housing Overlay zone within the mixed-use zoning district.  The Housing Overlay, per a code amendment in late 2025, now requires a minimum density of 30 units per acre and allows development by right if a residential development provides at least 20% affordable housing for lower income households. The City has also posted its housing site housing inventory list to indicate property suitable for development to help meet the City’s RHNA allocations. In 2024, the City commissioned a study determining the viability of raising the maximum densities within the Mixed-Use zone to spur development and attract higher quality MF projects. The City is currently in the process of updating the Mixed-Use zoning density based on the study. In 2025, the City Council voted to move forward with the recommendations of the study and expand the Mixed-Use zone while raising the maximum density to up to 90 units per acre, dependant on lot size. The code text and General Plan amendment which arose from those recommendations will be heard by the Planning commission on March 10, 2026 and the City Council in April or May of 2026.

PROGRAM_STATUS:
The City of Garden Grove Consolidated Plan is a planning document that identifies and develops a strategy to address critical housing and community development needs that can be addressed through federal funding sources, including Community Development Block Grant (CDBG), HOME Investment Partnerships (HOME), and Emergency Solutions Grants (ESG). The Consolidated Plan identifies strategies to support local organizations that provide emergency resources and provide opportunities for service expansion. 

In CY 2025, the City re-implemented the Emergency Solutions Grant Program for literally homeless or at-risk individuals through our ESG allocation. During CY 2025, the program has provided wrap-around services to over 180 homeless or at-risk individuals.

In partnership with Fountain Valley, Westminster, and Orange County, Garden Grove has developed a year-round Central Cities Navigation Center (CCNC), offering low-barrier transitional emergency housing and wrap-around services to homeless individuals in Orange County's Central Service Planning Area. The CCNC accommodates 85 beds with the capacity to expand to 100 beds. The CCNC opened on June 5, 2024 and has served a total of 386 individuals through December 31, 2025.

In 2022, the City adopted an ordinance to allow Low-Barrier Navigation Centers as a permitted use by right within the City’s Emergency Shelter Overlay Zone, to comply with State housing law.

In 2022, the City adopted an ordinance to allow transitional, supportive housing, and “supportive housing for homeless”, as permitted uses by-right in residential zoning districts subject to the same approval requirements, development standards, and restrictions that apply to other residential dwellings of the same type in the same zone, to comply with State housing law.

PROGRAM_NAME: Program 7: Preservation of Affordable Rental Housing
PROGRAM_OBJECTIVE:
Assist in the preservation of 280 affordable units at risk of converting to market rents by.

Periodically monitoring the status of the units that are at risk of converting to market rate during the planning period.

If any property owners indicate plans to convert affordable units to market rate rents, the City will contact qualified entities to explore transfer of ownership options. The entities will be selected from the State’s list of qualified entities to acquire/manage affordable housing. 

Make the State’s list of qualified entities to acquire/manage affordable housing available to interested residents, developers, or property owners. 

Inform residents in units that are converting to market rents of affordable housing programs available in the City, including Section 8 and other affordable housing developments.

Potentially provide financial assistance to owners of the Tamerlane Drive low-income housing units to preserve at-risk units.
PROGRAM_STATUS:
To assist in the preservation of affordable units at risk of converting to market rents, the City: periodically monitors the status of said units; contacts property owners of properties that are developed with at-risk units; makes the State’s list of qualified entities to acquire/manage affordable housing available to interested residents, developers, or property owners; when necessary, informs residents in units that are converting to market rents of affordable housing programs available in the City, including Section 8 and other affordable housing developments. 

The Orchard Grove project (formerly the Tamerlane Project) consists of 15 properties totaling 78 units. As of June 30, 2023, the affordability covenants for 10 of the properties (49 of the 78 units) had expired. The City worked with the owner and approved an Assignment and Assumption Agreement transferring all 15 properties to Affordable Housing Access, Inc. (AHA), a nonprofit corporation with a mission to create and preserve affordable housing. Subsequent to the approval and sale of the properties to AHA, the City approved an amendment to extend the affordability covenants for all expired properties and extended the affordability period until December 31, 2025.
AHA and the City executed a new Affordable Housing Agreement on February 5, 2024, which restates and restructures the terms and conditions for all 15 properties and resets the affordability period for all 78 units for a term of 55 years. During 2024 and 2025, AHA completed full interior rehabilitation of all 78 units. As of December 2025, all units are fully leased to low-income individuals and families.

The City is contracted with a Consultant who manages and monitors existing and new Density Bonus projects and agreements. In the event affordable units become at risk of converting to market rate units, the Consultant notifies City Staff, who then informs residents in units that are converting to market rents of affordable housing programs available in the City, including Section 8 and other affordable housing developments.

To bolster the program’s chances for success, the City will strengthen its relationship with the Regional Center of Orange County and foster new relationships with developers of supportive housing. This action has not been initiated yet due to the current lack of City resources.

PROGRAM_OBJECTIVE: Permit 10 ADUs each year on average (7 to 8 lower income each year on average, with 3 to 4 of these being affordable to extremely low income (no/low cost)); evaluate and identify appropriate pre-approved ADU site plans. Continue to track affordability during the permitting stage.
PROGRAM_STATUS:
On September 18th, 2025 the City Adopted Urgency Ordinance 25-11, related to Accessory Dwelling units and Junior Accessory Dwelling Units, in response to specific language changes to the City's most recent ADU Ordinance 25-04 provided by HCD. In such, Ordinance 25-11 is in compliance with State ADU Laws. 

Developed in 2024 and published January 2025, the City made available on its website "how to" submittal directions and a "pre-approved" ADU application to support streamlining ADU development in compliance with state law.

In 2025, the City received 8 entitlement applications, received 18 building permit applications, issued 13 building permits, and finaled 4 building permits for ADUs.

PROGRAM_OBJECTIVE: Identify at least 1 site and potential partner; and evaluate and pursue available funds; prioritize extremely low income households.
PROGRAM_STATUS: To augment its vacant and underutilized sites to accommodate the City’s lower income RHNA allocation, the City conducted a sites inventory in 2023 and identified existing multi-family housing and nonresidential sites. In July 2024, the City completed a vacant sites map utilizing 2023 land use data. The City will proceed to use the vacant and underutilized sites identified in the sites inventory to identify sites for RHNA credit allocation. The City will also seek funds substantial enough to make targeted units available for occupancy within two years of the agreement’s execution date. These actions have not been completed yet due to the current lack of City resources.

PROGRAM_OBJECTIVE: Maintaining consistency with state law.
PROGRAM_STATUS:
The City will ensure compliance with state law enacted through Senate Bill 330 and prohibit amendments to the General Plan or zoning of properties in a manner that would reduce residential density compared to the designation/district in effect as of January 1, 2018, without concurrent upzoning of equal capacity on property elsewhere in the City.

A Housing Projects Preliminary Application is available on the City's website for projects seeking vesting rights pursuant to SB 330. The form also serves as a referral to the Dana Point Planning Division for SB 330 vesting and streamlining purposes. In May 2024, staff reviewed the existing SB 330 application and deemed it consistent and current with state law. The City received 1 preliminary application in 2024, but a full application was never submitted within the required timeline so the SB 330 application expired.

PROGRAM_OBJECTIVE: Evaluate the effectiveness of in-lieu fees in the Coastal Zone and/or considering a citywide in-lieu fee, especially in comparison to other options; prioritize the creation of or assistance provided to extremely low income housing units when considering all options.
PROGRAM_STATUS: The City currently collects affordable housing in-lieu fees for units developed in the Headlands and Monarch Beach Resort Specific Plan, with additional in-lieu fees determined on a project-by-project basis. City staff will consider conducting a study of the in-lieu fee process in order to see how it can be applied to other projects city-wide. These actions have not been initiated yet due to the current lack of City resources.

PROGRAM_OBJECTIVE: Make annual contribution to support the development of affordable housing, homeless housing, and supportive housing throughout the county. Represent the interests of the City in discussions about the siting of proposed developments. OCHFT established a goal of 2,700 permanent supportive housing units to be developed throughout (in aggregate) member jurisdictions: 500 homeless families, 1,000 chronically homeless households, and 1,200 homeless individuals. These may or may not be located in Dana Point.
PROGRAM_STATUS: As a member, the City budgets $5,000 annually to contribute to the trust, which in turn is used to provide critical gap funding for the development of affordable housing, homeless housing, and supportive services solutions throughout the county.

PROGRAM_OBJECTIVE: The City will amend its zoning code to update its emergency shelter parking requirements as necessary to comply with recent changes to state law.
PROGRAM_STATUS: In November 2023, City Council had their first hearing for the proposed Zoning Code update. After a second reading, City Council adopted the ordinance on December 5th. The ordinance was certified by the California Coastal Commission on December 12, 2024.

PROGRAM_OBJECTIVE: Regularly update the City’s schedule of fees; evaluate the impact of waiving park and art in public places fees for lower income housing units in the next fee study.
PROGRAM_STATUS: The City anticipates conducting a fee study in the 2026-2027 fiscal year to ensure development fees are appropriate and consider possible reductions for special needs housing projects. The City continues to implement fee waivers for qualifying deed-restricted housing units affordable for lower income households and evaluate other options to further reduce costs for affordable housing in periodic updates, including options to facilitate more affordable housing in high resource areas.

PROGRAM_OBJECTIVE: Route the adopted Housing Element to the South Orange County Wastewater Authority and South Coast Water District and coordinate with both agencies on future housing projects and changes to the Housing Element.
PROGRAM_STATUS: The adopted Housing Element was sent to South Coast Water District and South Orange County Wastewater Authority. On July 24, 2024, City staff received confirmation that Priority Water and Sewer Services received the adopted Housing Element. The City will continue to coordinate with SCWD and SOCWA and adopt procedures to expedite service to lower income residential projects.

PROGRAM_OBJECTIVE: Maintain capacity to accommodate the unmet RHNA allocation on developable, adequately zoned sites throughout the entire planning period. Initiate a general plan update to expand opportunities to build new housing choices and expand affordability in high resource areas. Determine whether additional incentives are needed through the general plan update and/or subsequent changes to development standards to incentivize desired levels of affordability.
PROGRAM_STATUS: The City continues to monitor sites inventory and maintain adequate capacity. On May 3, 2022, City Council initiated the General Plan Update, which was conducted in two phases. The City completed Phase 1: Visioning Phase in 2023. The Visioning Phase consisted of a variety of in-person and virtual community engagement efforts, which was used to prepare a visioning framework document that will guide development of the General Plan Update in the next phase of the process. On November 4th, 2023, the City launched Phase 2: General Plan Development Phase, which took place throughout 2025. During Phase 2 in 2023, the City conducted a sites inventory identifying the City's vacant and under-utilized lots as part of the Land Use Element update. In July 2024, the City completed a vacant sites map utilizing 2023 land use data. The City continues to use the vacant and underutilized sites identified in the sites inventory and vacant sites map to identify adequate sites for RHNA allocation.

PROGRAM_OBJECTIVE: The City will amend its zoning code to permit low barrier navigation centers by right in nonresidential zones that permit multifamily and mixed use zones (per Government Code Sections 65660–65668, enacted through AB 101).
PROGRAM_STATUS: The City worked with the Orange County Council of Governments (OCCOG) for the development of model ordinances, including Low Barrier Navigation Centers per AB 101. This regional program is funded by the Regional Early Action Planning (REAP) grant awarded to OCCOG. City Council adopted this ordinance on December 5th, 2023, the ordinance was sent to the Coastal Commission on December 8, 2023, and certified by the Coastal Commission on December 12, 2024.

PROGRAM_OBJECTIVE: Maintain consistency with state law.
PROGRAM_STATUS: On September 18th, 2025 the City Adopted Urgency Ordinance 25-11, related to Accessory Dwelling units and Junior Accessory Dwelling Units, in response to specific language changes to the City's most recent ADU Ordinance 25-04 provided by HCD. In such, Ordinance 25-11 is in compliance with State ADU Laws.

PROGRAM_OBJECTIVE: Eliminate unnecessary constraints potentially created through the discretionary site development permit process.
PROGRAM_STATUS: The City will evaluate its site development permit process and requirements to identify and remove constraints to the production of housing. The evaluation will include interviews with planning staff in regard to their experiences with applicants subject to the site development permit process, including those who applied for but did not receive a site development permit. Based on this evaluation, the City will modify existing or establish new objective standards as part of the site development permit process to remove constraints to the production of housing. These actions have not been initiated yet due to the current lack of City resources.

PROGRAM_OBJECTIVE: Approve 20 to 50 lower income units in total on vacant and underutilized land.
PROGRAM_STATUS: The City adopted the code update of the City’s Density Bonus Ordinance to comply with state law, along with additional updates as necessary in response to new state law. The City is working with Orange County Council of Governments (OCCOG) for the development of model ordinances, including a Density Bonus Ordinance. This regional program is funded by the Regional Early Action Planning (REAP) grant awarded to OCCOG. The City proposes adopting the model ordinance provided by OCCOG and updating the City's existing density bonus in compliance with State regulations. Through the updated Density Bonus Ordinance, the City will encourage future housing projects to leverage density bonus provisions and provide affordable housing. In 2025, City staff re-reviewed the density bonus model ordinance and brought a draft ordinance to City Council for approval. It is anticipated that the ordinance will be certified by Coastal Commission in 2026.

PROGRAM_OBJECTIVE: Increase public awareness and information on energy conservation opportunities and assistance programs for new and existing residential units, and comply with state energy conservation requirements.
PROGRAM_STATUS:
The City continues to post and distribute information on currently available weatherization and energy conservation programs to residents and property owners through annual mailings in City utility billings, communication with community organizations and at municipal offices, and updates to the City’s website in the Housing Resource Directory. The City continues to enforce state requirements, including Title 24 of the California Code of Regulations, for energy conservation in new residential projects.

City staff continues to distribute housing resource information (including information on SDG&E's Energy Savings Program) to the public. Flyers and other informational resources created for housing resources were posted physically on public bulletin boards and shared digitally via the city website, social media posts, monthly newsletters, the Dana Point Lookout magazine, and slideshow presentations at City Council and Planning Commission meetings.

PROGRAM_OBJECTIVE: Update Municipal Code consistent with state law and produce residential project flow-chart and/or informational sheets, consistent with SB 35 and SB 330. Research and prepare options for consideration by the City Council to establish and implement an electronic/digital plan submittal and permit processing system to streamline the development process.
PROGRAM_STATUS: New laws (Senate Bills 35 and 330) were enacted to streamline review times for residential applications in an effort to stimulate and facilitate the construction of market rate and affordable housing. The City reviewed the new laws and determined an amendment to the Code was not required.  But, the City developed an application specific to SB330 to assist applicants and to streamline the permtting process. This regional program is funded by the Regional Early Action Planning (REAP) grant awarded to OCCOG. In February 2024, the City transitioned to an online plan submittal and permit processing system to streamline the development process. In June 2025, the City is transitioned to a fully electronic/digital permitting process.

PROGRAM_OBJECTIVE: Expand the use of vouchers in Dana Point to reduce the rate of overpayment in target areas and for target households. Connect interested landlords and qualifying tenants with the OCHA Program Administrator and the United Way WelcomeHomeOC program. Continue to coordinate with and FHC to increase outreach and promotional activities to increase awareness of voucher availability and relevant rules and laws. Emphasize increasing voucher use by extremely low income households. Increase voucher use by 50 tenants.
PROGRAM_STATUS:
The City will continue to implement the participation agreement with the Orange County Housing Authority (OCHA), which currently administers the Section 8 Certificate and Voucher Program for the City of Dana Point. The City will coordinate with the Orange County United Way on the WelcomeHomeOC program, which provides financial incentives, such as double security deposits, sign-on bonus, holding fees, and other assurances for landlords who rent units in Orange County, to individuals, veterans, and families with a housing voucher. The City will also coordinate with the Fair Housing Council (FHC) of Orange County to promote the use of vouchers by current and prospective tenants and the acceptance of vouchers by landlords. 

19 OCHA tenants have utilized their housing choice voucher in Dana Point in 2025. 

City staff continues to distribute housing resource information to the public. Flyers created for housing resources were posted on public bulletin boards. Electronic distribution were made via the city website, social media posts, monthly newsletters, the Dana Point Lookout magazine, and slideshow presentations at City Council and Planning Commission meetings.

PROGRAM_NAME: 6.6 Residential Care Facilities, Six or Fewer Persons
PROGRAM_OBJECTIVE: Ensure consistency with state law.
PROGRAM_STATUS: In December 2022, City staff began drafting proposed code language revisions to ensure that it is clear that a CUP is not required for group homes for six or fewer people (residential care facilities), consistent with the City’s position in compliance with state law (particularly Health & Safety Code Section 11834.23). City Council adopted the Zone Text Amendment with the specified definition on December 5th, 2023. The amendment was sent to Coastal Commission on December 8, 2023, and certified by the Coastal Commission on December 12, 2024.

PROGRAM_OBJECTIVE: Connect qualifying homebuyers with the County of Orange MCC and MAP Program Administrator. Coordinate with the County on an annual basis to increase awareness of programs through expanded marketing and promotional materials distributed in Dana Point (particularly in census tracts where rates of rental overpayment are high).
PROGRAM_STATUS: The City maintains its agreement with the County of Orange to administer the program. The City continues the program with Orange County Housing Authority. In 2025, the County had no MAP homebuyers purchasing in Dana Point.

PROGRAM_OBJECTIVE: Continue to collect in-lieu fees and support Mary Erickson Community Housing in operating the Housing Initiatives Program. Assist 20 hotel employees who are Dana Point residents annually. Prepare analysis of feasibility to apply similar requirements to future hotels.
PROGRAM_STATUS: In 2025, 27 Dana Point hotel employees received rental subsidies. The City will consider an expansion of the program to apply toward the development of new hotels.

PROGRAM_OBJECTIVE: Ensure compliance with City codes, with a focus on substandard housing in low resource areas, which includes garage conversions and unpermitted additions.
PROGRAM_STATUS: The Code Enforcement Division promotes, maintains, and enforces ordinances and laws to preserve, protect, and enhance the quality of life in Dana Point. Code Compliance officers actively work with community members and neighborhood organizations in assuring the City remains a healthy and welcoming place to live, work, and visit. The City recognizes the importance of community wide code compliance and has made it one of the focuses of the latest strategic plan update.

PROGRAM_OBJECTIVE: Adopt affordability monitoring as a condition of approval for affordable housing projects and distribute educational materials on affordable housing conversion to the public at City Hall and through the City website.
PROGRAM_STATUS:
The Community Development annually monitors deed-restricted units through its own records and external databases. All current income-restricted housing projects are preserved in perpetuity. For future projects, the City will continue to encourage preservation in perpetuity but include affordable housing monitoring as a condition of approval for projects with time-limited affordable housing component. 

The City continues its program of annual monitoring and provide ongoing preservation technical assistance and educational materials to affected tenants and the community at large on the need to preserve the existing affordable housing stock through brochures at City Hall.

PROGRAM_OBJECTIVE: Refer persons in need of housing assistance to the Fair Housing Council of Orange County and other community housing resources.
PROGRAM_STATUS:
The City maintains a Housing Resources Directory, which includes a directory of contacts for housing-related assistance, including contact telephone numbers in Orange County and website links where persons may inquire about equal or fair housing. The City communicates with the Fair Housing Council of Orange County, Legal Aid, and other non-profit housing groups to maintain the directory. The City also provides a link to the housing information programs and the directory of contacts on the City’s website.

City staff continues to distribute housing resource information to the public. Flyers and other informational resources created for housing resources were posted physically on public bulletin boards and shared digitally via the city website, social media posts, monthly newsletters, the Dana Point Lookout magazine, and slideshow presentations at City Council and Planning Commission meetings.

PROGRAM_OBJECTIVE: The City will amend its zoning code to permit supportive housing by right in zones where multifamily and mixed uses are permitted (per Government Code Sections 65583(c)(3), enacted through AB 2162).
PROGRAM_STATUS: The City initiated research for the code update in December 2022 and looked into other cities’ ordinances in compliance with AB 2162. The City worked with the Orange County Council of Governments (OCCOG) for the development of model ordinances, including Supportive Housing per AB 2162. This regional program is funded by the Regional Early Action Planning (REAP) grant awarded to OCCOG. City Council adopted this ordinance on December 5th, 2023. The ordinance was sent to the Coastal Commission on December 8, 2023 and certified in December 12, 2024. The ordinance states that supportive housing projects would be permitted in all zones where multifamily and mixed use are permitted.

PROGRAM_OBJECTIVE: Inform Dana Point residents, property owners, and real estate agents of condominium conversion requirements through the City’s website.
PROGRAM_STATUS: The City’s Zoning Code (Section 9.09.040 Special Development Standards) has requirements for condominium conversions that address issues of concern. The City continues to enforce its current regulations and make appropriate modifications, as necessary, such as additional considerations for conversions in low and high resource areas.

PROGRAM_NAME: 2.4 Conversion to Affordable or Permanent Supportive Housing
PROGRAM_OBJECTIVE: Approve 10 units of extremely low income housing through conversion.
PROGRAM_STATUS: Similar to the efforts taken to create the Silver Lantern permanent transitional housing (17 units), the City will coordinate with entities to evaluate the feasibility of converting a nonresidential use into affordable housing, such as single room occupancy (SRO) units or permanent supportive housing. Extremely low-income households will be prioritized with affordability protected in perpetuity if feasible, but for no less than 55 years. These actions have not been initiated yet due to the current lack of City resources.

PROGRAM_OBJECTIVE: Assist 2-4 lower income households annually, up to a total of 20 households.
PROGRAM_STATUS:
The City continues to be a sub-recipient to the County of Orange for CDBG and HOME funds so that Dana Point households will remain eligible to participate in the programs. 

While no rehabilitation projects were initiated through this program in 2025, the City will continue to be a sub-receipient for CDBG through the County to implement housing rehabilitation programs. The City will also coordinate with the County to prioritize the expenditure of funding on housing occupied by lower income households in low resource areas with an emphasis on place-based revitalization.

The City's agreement with the County of Orange for the CDBG program was renewed in closed in July 2023 and is good for three years.

PROGRAM_OBJECTIVE: Assist 2-4 lower income housing units annually, up to a total of 20 households. Explore the feasibility of redirecting housing in-lieu fees to support additional rental rehabilitation efforts.
PROGRAM_STATUS:
The County offers rental rehabilitation funding for various housing types, including multifamily and mobile homes. The City continues to be a sub-recipient to the County for CDBG to implement housing rehabilitation programs to address health and safety needs and preserve the existing housing stock.

While no rehabilitation projects were initiated in 2025, the City is evaluating the feasibility of redirecting housing in-lieu funds towards the rehabilitation of existing rental units, such as the Domingo/Doheny Apartments, to strengthen the program’s chances of success. The City will coordinate with the County to prioritize the expenditure of funding on housing occupied by lower income households in low resource areas with an emphasis on place-based revitalization.

PROGRAM_OBJECTIVE: Identify critical neighborhood improvements for inclusion in annual CIP and proactively monitor neighborhood conditions, with priority for low resource areas.
PROGRAM_STATUS: The City maintains a Neighborhood Maintenance and Improvement Guide and has a Capital Improvements Program that helps to revitalize infrastructure. The City will prioritize the expenditure of funding in neighborhoods occupied by lower income households in low resource areas with an emphasis on place-based revitalization.

On Seotember 19, 2025 the City adopted Urgency Ordinance 25-12 repealing Ordinance No.22-01, which added chapter 9.72 (Regulating Urban Lot Splits) to the City of Dana Point Municipal Code, and prohibiting uses conflicting with the City's Council's contemplated adoption of regulations repealing the forgoing which were adopted to implement SB 9.
